Conversations: groups of 2-6, up to ten attachments x 10 MB with checksums installed without following symlinks; reply threads use separate native sessions; mentions identify participants; recipient owns the request.
Work panel derives state from runtime events; Stop cancels descendants and waits for executors; Retry creates a new operation after settle; uncertain execution blocks replay.
Artifacts immutable in MinIO with checksums, 10 MB; file bytes travel through runtime adapter, not model arguments.
Automatic intake applies to /api/v1/messages with intent auto; legacy intents and /api/v1/tasks keep old behaviour.

Coordination semantics: hermbot_message (nonblocking inbox), hermbot_delegate (contribution or deliverable, returns immediately), hermbot_wait (named waits, releases capacity), replaces_task_id replacement of settled failures only.

Acceptance: hermbot_finish with review and reviewed contributions; file contributions need a hermbot_read_artifact receipt; acceptances bind requirement revision, artifact version/checksum and review.

Grants and lifecycle proposals: standing grants with targets/ops/expiry/budget; revocation stops operations using the grant; approved lifecycle operations go to a durable supervisor outbox; ambiguous receipts stay in reconciliation.
Runtime ownership: per-bot network/identity/credential/volumes; only supervisor has Docker socket; API and worker attach to bot networks; DB/storage on control network; only 127.0.0.1:8780 published.
Compose owns API, worker, supervisor, PostgreSQL, MinIO and runtime-image helper; legacy fixed runtime services kept under 'legacy' profile (list omits event-worker and notification-worker).

Hermes pinned to revision 749220ef / digest d4da4a40 with no upstream source patches; llm_request and tool_execution middleware; read-only root FS, root-owned plugin dir, no effective caps; Rollup pinned 4.62.2 because 4.64.0 exhausted memory.

Execution defaults: 3 concurrent executions, one active/uncertain attempt per bot, depth 3, ten handoffs; no 5-min cutoff or 20-min deadline; 60 active minutes budget; Continue adds allowance; pre-tool transient failures recover at most twice.
Execution assessments are optional/async and never grant access or declare completion; Decisions via /decisions vs structured /chat/completions alternative.

Computer: browser.backend off keeps built-in browser tools; desktop memory floor 1,024 MB; takeover with native lease/epoch; secure input via live connection, not stored.

Concurrent tool admission: takeover closes new admission and drains admitted callbacks; per-bot barrier owned by Hermbot.

extra_nodes.purpose: Every issue in plan/ISSUES.md (C00-C65, review-table IDs, KAG/STAR/TEMP/RET/CTRL/GATE/COORD, H01-H03, M01-M28) with cause, fix, status and owning feature.

issues.title: Plan mode would not turn off in the original planning thread
issues.cause: Issue/cause: The owner reported that plan mode was not turning off and directed implementation from a new thread. This was a tooling/workflow obstacle, before Hermbot usage, rather than an application defect.
issues.fix: Approach and outcome: Preserve the original plan and transcript, transfer context and begin implementation in the next thread.
issues.status: Workflow recovered by starting the implementation thread; underlying Codex behavior not diagnosed.

issues.title: Initial collaboration tools were not directly available
issues.cause: Issue/cause: Hermes deferred plugin tools by default.
issues.fix: Approach and outcome: Expose the small collaboration toolset directly.
issues.status: Historically corrected

issues.title: Native session creation conflicted on titles
issues.cause: Issue/cause: Session titles needed to be unique within a runtime.
issues.fix: Approach and outcome: Use session-specific titles.
issues.status: Historically corrected

issues.title: Frontend build exhausted machine memory
issues.cause: Issue/cause: An automatically resolved Rollup version exhausted memory on this machine.
issues.fix: Approach and outcome: Pin the verified build dependency rather than depending on the newest resolution.
issues.status: Historically corrected

issues.title: Request ID generation failed on plain HTTP
issues.cause: Issue/cause: Browser request-ID generation depended on functionality unavailable on the local plain-HTTP origin.
issues.fix: Approach and outcome: Generate IDs with cryptographically generated bytes compatible with that environment.
issues.status: Historically corrected

issues.title: Long group list overflowed mobile navigation
issues.cause: Issue/cause: The initial sidebar could not accommodate a long group list.
issues.fix: Approach and outcome: Scrollable groups with reachable owner controls; later roster redesign addressed competition among sections.
issues.status: Historically corrected; later expanded by C06/C07

issues.title: Attachment extraction could follow a bot-created workspace symlink.
issues.cause: Attachment extraction could follow a bot-created workspace symlink.
issues.fix: Stage in a root-owned image directory; install with directory descriptors and `O_NOFOLLOW`, checksum verification and atomic replacement.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: Clone helpers initialized new data-volume roots with root ownership.
issues.cause: Clone helpers initialized new data-volume roots with root ownership.
issues.fix: Set both target mount roots to the native Hermes user before copying selected state.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: Raw SQLite copying could lose committed WAL data, and read-only source mounts could prevent creation of SQLite's WAL index.
issues.cause: Raw SQLite copying could lose committed WAL data, and read-only source mounts could prevent creation of SQLite's WAL index.
issues.fix: Pause the source; copy database/WAL into isolated scratch storage; use SQLite backup into the target.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: Failed or ambiguously created clone helpers could prevent retry or hold deleted volumes.
issues.cause: Failed or ambiguously created clone helpers could prevent retry or hold deleted volumes.
issues.fix: Validate full ownership labels, resume created helpers, recreate settled failed helpers and remove owned helpers during deletion.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: Provisioning reported success immediately after container creation, including a runtime that was failing to start.
issues.cause: Provisioning reported success immediately after container creation, including a runtime that was failing to start.
issues.fix: Wait for Docker runtime health; preserve partial state and return actionable failure details.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: A restarting runtime could fail deletion because the stop check covered only `running`.
issues.cause: A restarting runtime could fail deletion because the stop check covered only `running`.
issues.fix: Stop both running and restarting containers before removal.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: Rebuilt image tags could reuse a container created from old image contents.
issues.cause: Rebuilt image tags could reuse a container created from old image contents.
issues.fix: Include the resolved image identity in the configuration fingerprint.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: A lost provisioning receipt could repeat a completed lifecycle effect after supervisor recovery.
issues.cause: A lost provisioning receipt could repeat a completed lifecycle effect after supervisor recovery.
issues.fix: Persist payload hashes/results atomically on a dedicated supervisor volume, fsync file/directory, replay receipts, and clean clone helpers on replay.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: Approved creation retry incorrectly spent or checked a second creation budget; a settled manager could reuse old authority.
issues.cause: Approved creation retry incorrectly spent or checked a second creation budget; a settled manager could reuse old authority.
issues.fix: Recheck live authority without consuming another creation, reject settled manager operations and stale/source-busy retries.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.cause: Provider/timezone changes could unarchive a bot, and saved timezone changes were not applied to runtimes.

issues.title: A renamed provider could be reimported from `.env` after restart.

issues.title: Link import could reach private infrastructure through redirects or DNS changes, and a continuously dripping response could defeat socket t…
issues.cause: Link import could reach private infrastructure through redirects or DNS changes, and a continuously dripping response could defeat socket timeouts.
issues.fix: Validate all resolved addresses at every redirect, connect to the validated numeric IP, verify TLS against the original hostname, and avoid environment proxies. Bound redirects/bytes and interrupt response headers/body at a wall-clock deadline.
issues.status: Historically corrected within source review scope

issues.title: Chromium blocked PDF previews inside a sandboxed frame.
issues.cause: Chromium blocked PDF previews inside a sandboxed frame.
issues.fix: Serve PDF with fixed `application/pdf`, `nosniff` and same-origin framing policy so the built-in viewer works. Other content retains the restrictive sandbox policy.

issues.cause: Native memory writes could follow unsafe directories/files or hang on a FIFO; concurrent CAS could overwrite another edit.
issues.fix: Use directory/file descriptors with `O_NOFOLLOW`, require regular UTF-8 files, use nonblocking file opens, and serialize writes with a cross-process lock and atomic fsynced replacement.

issues.title: Invalid bot configuration could be rejected after native knowledge had already changed; a skill description could have a non-string YAML va…

issues.cause: Hermes caches memory/skill configuration, so saving disk content alone did not guarantee the next model run saw it.

issues.title: Native completion prose could misstate recurring success
issues.cause: Observed/design defect: A manager could end a native turn without accepted required results while the execution itself recorded completion. Original-root-only failure counting also missed later successful repair of the same occurrence.
issues.fix: Approach/fix: Reject final acceptance while required or optional automated work is unsettled. If a manager ends without accepted required results, record explicit failure and stop remaining owned execution. Count definite failures from current settled occurrence work/results. Advance incremental windows only from verified compatible success, including equivalent grant renewal, and after attempts/effects settle.
issues.status: Fixed with missing-result/failure regressions, final acceptance guards and verified native contribution receipts.

issues.title: Managed reply admission could invert revocation's lock order
issues.cause: Observed/design defect: The newly authority-bound peer path could validate/hold a grant before acquiring its work lock, while revocation acquired work before updating the grant. Those two orders can wait on each other.
issues.fix: Approach/fix: Claim canonical work/root nonblockingly before validating authority in peer admission. Align dispatch/revoke canonical work identity and skip a busy occurrence for a later pass. Replies inherit scope/run/thread/budget; revocation cancels owned pending execution and messages without fabricating effect receipts.
issues.status: Fixed; concurrent revoke/claim and locked-occurrence peer-admission regressions pass.

issues.title: Push timeout extension changed the existing connector deadline

issues.status: Fixed; the original slow-drip transport regression and cumulative 638-test suite pass.

issues.title: Catch-up eligibility could use unrelated unread work
issues.cause: Observed/design defect: A summary whose own covered questions had resolved could still send because a different unread question existed elsewhere.
issues.fix: Approach/fix: Recheck actual covered item/version references and their freshness; overflow summaries alone represent general fresh backlog. Do not self-merge a summary into itself.

issues.title: Quiet-period and overflow replacement could repeat or lose interruption
issues.cause: Observed/design defect: Repeated local hours could yield two quiet-end keys. Preference changes could suppress a pending summary after its individual records were marked covered; overflow-only backlog had no item row to recreate.
issues.fix: Approach/fix: Key quiet periods by explicit local period/policy/browser generation; retain fresh covered members and one overflow obligation across policy replacement. Reserve one of 1,000 pending positions for overflow and count actual dispatch attempts for the three-per-minute cap. Do not replay stale work or drop the in-app record.
issues.status: Fixed; DST-fold, covered-member policy replacement, saturation, burst and overflow-only replacement regressions pass.

issues.title: Slow push could delay the attention projector
issues.cause: Observed/design defect: The first notification worker performed projection and outbound delivery sequentially, so a slow vendor could hold new inbox state behind HTTP.

issues.title: Retention could reverse the delivery lock order
issues.cause: Observed/design defect: Delivery completion acquired delivery before subscription/preferences, while initial reconciliation/retention held preferences/subscriptions before updating expired deliveries. An expiring in-flight record can complete that cycle.
issues.fix: Approach/fix: Commit maintenance families independently; derive server-key health from subscription state rather than updating preferences while holding a delivery lock. Use fenced short claims and send outside transactions.

issues.cause: OutcomeSpec records only broad `artifact` kind, and claim validation accepts an accessible artifact without checking requested format/delivery. The review expressly disclosed that the actual ZIP was local.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): distinguish supporting evidence from the deliverable; bind acceptance to the actual downloadable file and relevant contract conditions.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Derived ZIP stayed fulfilled after upstream changes
issues.cause: dependency readiness checks status by key, without recording the upstream accepted revision used to build a derived output. Revising website content did not invalidate the earlier ZIP acceptance.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): record derivation/version relationships and mark affected outputs stale when their inputs change. Preserve immutable historical external effects; do not automatically resend Slack because content changed.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Slack completion linked a private container path
issues.cause: the bot used a local path after ZIP publication failed. A provider receipt validates posting, not recipient access to a mentioned file. M04/M05 allowed this misleading completion state.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): base delivery notifications on the accepted actual deliverable and accurately describe access; a private application link also must not be assumed accessible to a colleague.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Published website assets lost their relationships
issues.cause: HTML used local relative filenames while separate published artifacts had different names. Local browser verification tested a different package from the downloaded output.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): deliver a coherent archive or self-contained document using existing publication, and verify the exported package from a clean directory. Website hosting is not implicitly part of this fix.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Descriptive titles used as extensionless filenames
issues.cause: filename validation and download response accept a safe arbitrary name and use it unchanged; display title and usable filename are conflated.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): preserve/validate the actual filename and keep descriptive labeling separate where needed; define behavior for missing or conflicting extensions.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Reopen retained cancelled requirements
issues.cause: register resets status only when descriptive fields differ. Identical requirements remain cancelled, and the intake contract has no explicit reopening transition.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): an explicit owner-requested lifecycle transition independent of text edits; define fulfilled/uncertain external-effect handling before implementation.
issues.status: Open; reproduced.

issues.title: Normal confirmations failed strict choice matching
issues.cause: the interpreter asked for an exact choice after “done, move forward”; answer also rejects punctuation variants because it requires literal equality. Ordinary conversational answers and exact action approvals need different semantics.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): associate the actual answer with the identified question and normalize unambiguous ordinary choices while preserving original text; retain exact approval requirements for consequential actions.
issues.status: Open; exact comparison reproduced, historical rejection cause partly uncertain.

issues.title: Clarification requested already available course information
issues.cause: the saved interpretation at 593 asserted missing course information despite earlier course context remaining inside the history window. M27 promoted that mistake into the executing bot's immediate instruction. This is not proven context-window exhaustion.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): resolve references against recorded work and available conversation facts before asking; preserve uncertainty instead of asserting unsupported absence.
issues.status: Open; erroneous interpretation confirmed, model's internal cause unknown.

issues.title: Confirmations repeatedly requested
issues.cause: conversational clarifications and durable input requests have inconsistent answer tracking. Some scope confirmations were saved correctly but later executions reconsidered them; this is not evidence the database lost them.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): consistently associate questions, answers and resolved scope with the work; reuse answers unless a material change makes them insufficient.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Delayed acknowledgement answered a newer question
issues.cause: answer handling resumes the origin and separately queues acknowledgement; question context is task-local, and worker sessions persist per bot/conversation. The acknowledgement lacks its answered-question receipt while seeing newer session history.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): make acknowledgement refer explicitly to its question/answer and avoid a separate unconstrained agent execution for a routine receipt.
issues.status: Open; mechanism reproduced.

issues.title: Duplicate acknowledgements queued behind long work
issues.cause: answer-plus-update produces multiple executions in intake. One active attempt per bot and oldest-task-first scheduling let the resumed original work finish before acknowledgements. Message 605 received responses approximately 42 minutes later.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): apply the answer/update once and produce one appropriate acknowledgement without competing execution jobs. Preserve one active bot execution; raising concurrency alone is not a solution.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Owner-facing clarification sent to a teammate
issues.cause: Quill chose peer messaging and described Scout as “researcher/owner.” Coordination authorizes peers correctly but does not establish that the owner received an answer.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): carry explicit response audience/provenance and distinguish peer consultation from answering the user. Avoid disabling legitimate discussion-time peer consultation.
issues.status: Open; bot audience-selection error confirmed.

issues.title: Failed intake became “owner did not authorize”
issues.cause: failed newer requests created no work changes/authorization, and the later peer task was unlinked to work. Execution context exposed processed instructions; the bot treated absence of recorded authority as absence of an owner request.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): surface a pending/failed interpretation distinctly from a missing request. Repair intake before execution rather than treating raw failed proposals as permission.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Mistyped internal reply ID escalated to owner
issues.cause: actual message ID ended `60d9ece3`; the bot submitted `60e9ece3`. Reply validation correctly rejected it with a generic 403 also used for scope failures. Recovery was incorrectly delegated to the owner.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): select exact scoped references from the inbox and return actionable, privacy-preserving reference feedback; never ask the user to repair internal UUIDs.
issues.status: Open; exact trigger confirmed from Hermes history.

issues.title: Help request got only an acknowledgement
issues.cause: the “Need help” choice resumed work still affected by M10 and created an acknowledgement-only turn. Routing told the latter to acknowledge and finish; it could do so without providing the requested instructions.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): treat a request for help as substantive content to answer, associated with the original obstacle, rather than only an answer receipt.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: Interactive vault prompt unavailable in API execution
issues.cause: upstream `browser_vault_save_login()` returns `prompt_unavailable` without an interactive callback. Hermbot exposed the native tool in its headless/API execution; repeated calls could not create that surface. Hermes correctly reported the limitation.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): supply accurate runtime guidance and use a supported secure-input path or supported callback integration. Keep credentials outside chat and Hermes source unchanged; no blanket native-tool blocking is authorized.
issues.status: Open integration/recovery gap; harness limitation confirmed.

issues.title: Slack write attempted before required ZIP was ready
issues.cause: delegated Slack task had no task dependencies and started immediately, while outcome dependencies were enforced at dispatch. The bot attempted the write rather than preparing then waiting. Task delegation and outcome readiness express different dependencies.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): make prerequisite readiness explicit to the responsible execution and support preparation followed by an actual dependency wait. Do not require all preparatory work to wait unnecessarily.
issues.status: Open orchestration behavior; protective guard worked.

issues.title: Earlier broad “poor revision recovery” finding corrected
issues.cause: revision rejections occurred in one batch over about 35 ms; status read succeeded roughly eight seconds later. This does not demonstrate a persistent retry loop. One denied artifact existed in previous work but was not granted to its replacement; another supplied artifact ID did not exist.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): preserve correct revision/access guards; evaluate recovery per actual cause. Reference usability belongs with M18/M23. No fix is claimed or required for the alleged persistent loop without new evidence.
issues.status: Corrected finding, 2026-10-13 investigation.

issues.title: Invalid tool schema and contribution references
issues.cause: action arguments supplied to discovery-only `hermbot_connectors`; required `result` omitted from finish; old root tasks supplied as current contribution IDs. These were observed invalid calls, not proof that published schemas were wrong.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): use exact discovered references and clear argument/recovery contracts; review duplicated schema definitions for drift before attributing errors to them.
issues.status: Open reliability issue; validators worked.

issues.title: Retry lacked application rejection feedback
issues.cause: schema feedback occurs inside `interpret()`, but application validation in `apply()` runs afterward. Its exception starts another attempt without the rejected proposal or precise rejection feedback. See intake.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): return structured application validation to a bounded repair flow against fresh state; distinguish transient conflicts from invalid proposals and preserve transaction/authorization guarantees.
issues.status: Open; code confirmed.

issues.title: Intake failure details discarded
issues.cause: the exception handler avoids storing sensitive provider responses but also drops safe application failure details. Recorded 33 retries and 12 failures expose `HTTPException` without its cause.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): retain structured sanitized error codes, failure stage and correlation/revision metadata sufficient to diagnose and repair; preserve privacy by design, not by logging complete proposals/transcripts.
issues.status: Open.

issues.title: New executions silently inherited legacy semantics
issues.cause: create_task defaults coordination version to zero; derived intake and UI-answer creation omit it. A compatibility rule can propagate the downgrade. This is not the cause of M03/M05, whose acceptances used version 1.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): make current/inherited execution semantics explicit at every constructor; confine legacy behavior to genuine legacy work without silently rewriting historical evidence.
issues.status: Open; reproduced and confirmed in production metadata.

issues.title: Clarification replaced immediate owner input
issues.cause: intake stores clarification in `continuation`; worker uses `continuation or input`. Original text remains stored but the immediate request becomes an instruction to ask the interpreter's question.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): preserve the authenticated user message and represent interpretation/clarification separately with its provenance; avoid having a second model blindly execute a mistaken clarification as the user's request.
issues.status: Open; reproduced.

issues.title: Chat credential copied into execution records
issues.cause: ordinary task creation stores the submitted message as task input, and execution copies it into attempts. Secure input protects its separate path, not credentials pasted into ordinary chat.
issues.fix: PROPOSED (not implemented): define handling for accidental chat secrets, minimize downstream propagation, and provide a secure replacement path. Existing-record cleanup and credential rotation require a concrete scoped plan; this documentation does not perform them.
issues.status: Open.

decisions.decision: Grok Bot-style product with Hermes underneath; one bot per container/runtime; private workspace; web first; local POC then Linux server; review external writes; Google/Slack/GitHub/MCP/browser; close UX fidelity; owner-managed providers; management = tasks and lifecycle
OpenAI-compatible APIs first; Codex/Claude subscriptions later

Finish Phase 5 first; mobile use as Phase 6A between 6 and 7

One bot = one container = one persistent Hermes runtime with private data/workspace/browser volumes.
decisions.why: Owner requirement (P-U6) for independent runtimes that communicate like Grok Bot teammates; per-bot runtime/volume/browser isolation is stronger than the reference product's shared computer.
decisions.alternatives: Hermes profiles inside one runtime (profiles are not filesystem boundaries); Hermes terminal Docker sandbox only; shared cloud computer like Grok Bot; VM per bot (deferred).
decisions.tradeoffs: More memory/CPU per bot and lifecycle machinery (supervisor, clone helpers); stronger isolation and independent recovery.

decisions.decision: Only the supervisor holds the Docker socket, behind an authenticated internal interface; agents never get it.
decisions.why: Containers/limits/upgrades are infrastructure authority that must not be reachable from agents or the public API.
decisions.alternatives: API or worker owning Docker directly; agents with socket access.
decisions.tradeoffs: Extra service/hop and a durable outbox for lifecycle operations; tight blast-radius control.

decisions.decision: Provisioning reports success only after Docker runtime health and applied-revision readiness; readiness cleared when a lifecycle change is queued.
decisions.why: A container that was created but failing to start had been reported as success (P2-05/P2-15).

decisions.decision: Supervisor persists lifecycle payload hashes/results atomically (fsync file + directory) on its own volume and replays receipts; changed payload for same operation is rejected.
decisions.why: A lost provisioning receipt could repeat a completed lifecycle effect after supervisor recovery (P2-08).
decisions.alternatives: Stateless supervisor relying on DB only.

decisions.decision: Clone copies only explicitly selected state (memories, skill files, workspace, native history) with fresh identities/tokens/volumes; SQLite copied via backup API from a paused source; browser state and credential files excluded.
decisions.why: Raw SQLite copy could lose committed WAL data; credentials/browser logins must never be silently duplicated.
decisions.alternatives: Full volume copy; copying browser profiles.
decisions.tradeoffs: Source bot pauses during clone; clones lack logins.

decisions.decision: Configuration fingerprint includes resolved image identity; configuration/provider/timezone changes apply only between runs; archive status frozen in the outbox.
decisions.why: Rebuilt image tags reused stale containers; config could unarchive bots (P2-07/P2-10).
decisions.tradeoffs: Owners must let work settle or explicitly stop it.

decisions.decision: Delete requires typing the exact name and removes runtime/private volumes, while task records and published artifacts stay readable under Past teammates.
decisions.why: Deletion is destructive and owner-only; history must survive.

decisions.decision: Runtime containers run with read-only root filesystem, root-owned managed plugin, CapDrop ALL + no-new-privileges; bootstrap drops to the Hermes UID.
decisions.why: Native tools could otherwise replace runtime code or the managed extension once connection-based tool blocking was removed.
decisions.tradeoffs: Attachment staging needed Docker Exec into /run/hermbot-staging.

decisions.decision: On restart the worker reconnects network endpoints and only starts runtimes whose desired state is running; archived/stopped stay stopped.
decisions.why: Runtime desired state is distinct from task activity.
decisions.tradeoffs: docker compose stop alone leaves bot containers running.

[status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

[status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

[status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

P2-12 — Pending work could be admitted while lifecycle configuration was taking effect; some lock orders could form cycles.: Pending work could be admitted while lifecycle configuration was taking effect; some lock orders could form cycles. → Fence task/delegation admission with a shared bot lock using `NOWAIT`; use workspace-before-source order for clone, root-before-grant for revocation, and nonblocking target locks for exact lifecycle approval. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

P2-15 — Readiness from a prior configuration could appear current during provisioning.: Readiness from a prior configuration could appear current during provisioning. → Clear readiness when queuing lifecycle changes and wait for the applied revision in browser acceptance. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

decisions.decision: The browser never drives execution; one authoritative server-side transcript/driver per room; closing the client doesn't stop work.
decisions.why: Groups and background work must continue after the app closes.
decisions.alternatives: Client-driven turn-taking; Hermes native desktop relay rooms.
decisions.tradeoffs: Backend must own group scheduling and recovery.

decisions.decision: Groups support 2-6 teammates; cap enforced also at specialist-approval time; membership removal blocked while native work is unresolved.
decisions.why: Roadmap default group size; P2-14 found approval could exceed cap.

decisions.decision: Attachments are bound to their conversation, checksummed and installed into the recipient's workspace via root-owned staging with O_NOFOLLOW descriptors; up to ten files x 10 MB.
decisions.why: Bot-created symlinks could redirect extraction (P2-01).

decisions.decision: Reply threads use separate native sessions; mentions only identify participants while the selected recipient owns the request.
decisions.why: Keep thread context separate; avoid mentions silently creating assignments.

decisions.decision: Group removal archives (archived_at) after settled-work checks, retaining records/outputs, with restore.
decisions.why: Owner wanted fixture cleanup without losing history (C14).

decisions.decision: Client request IDs generated with crypto.getRandomValues (requestKey) rather than crypto.randomUUID.
decisions.why: randomUUID is unavailable on the plain-HTTP local origin (C04, repeated C44).

decisions.decision: Sidebar sections collapsible with remembered state in browser storage; single roster scroll area.
decisions.why: Three fixed-height sections hid groups (C07).

[status: Historically corrected]

C05 — Long group list overflowed mobile navigation: Issue/cause: The initial sidebar could not accommodate a long group list. → Approach and outcome: Scrollable groups with reachable owner controls; later roster redesign addressed competition among sections. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

P2-14 — Group membership edits could remove a teammate with uncertain execution; approved specialist creation could exceed the group cap.: Group membership edits could remove a teammate with uncertain execution; approved specialist creation could exceed the group cap. → Block removal while native work is unresolved and check the six-member limit at approval. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

P2-16 — Settings forms submitted database-only fields, and some browser state survived retired bots, pagination, session expiry or changed conversa…: Settings forms submitted database-only fields, and some browser state survived retired bots, pagination, session expiry or changed conversations. → Send explicit settings fields; guard repeated settings submissions; recover active conversations and expired login; scope uploads to their original conversation; reset pagination and streamed text between runs. P2-17 — Deleting a bot hid its retained direct chat, and state windows could hide old unsettled work or conversation outputs.: Deleting a bot hid its retained direct chat, and state windows could hide old unsettled work or conversation outputs. → Add read-only past-teammate navigation, preserve unresolved work in the state projection, and load all outputs for the selected conversation. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

P3-14 — A late knowledge/file response could populate or close a panel after switching teammates/conversations.: A late knowledge/file response could populate or close a panel after switching teammates/conversations. → Scope callback generations to the panel opening and target; retain the original operation while suppressing stale draft, file-chip, error and busy-state updates. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

P3-15 — New group selection could reset to an older chat before its metadata reached the cache.: New group selection could reset to an older chat before its metadata reached the cache. → Refresh the conversation roster before selecting the new group, so active-conversation recovery sees the new ID. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

C07 — Three noncollapsible roster sections hid groups: Issue/cause: Separate fixed-height scroll areas competed for limited sidebar height; footer could escape short screens. → Approach and outcome: Collapsible remembered sections, temporary search expansion, one roster scroll region and retained footer. [status: Verified within recorded viewports; same issue as H03]

UI-02 — Teammates, past teammates and groups competed for fixed heights in separate scroll areas; the footer could extend below short viewports.: Teammates, past teammates and groups competed for fixed heights in separate scroll areas; the footer could extend below short viewports. → Add independent accessible section toggles and remember their state in browser storage. Past teammates starts collapsed. Search reveals matching sections temporarily. Use one roster scroll area and a fixed-size footer. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

[status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

UI-04 — Loading a conversation briefly displayed the empty-chat welcome.: Loading a conversation briefly displayed the empty-chat welcome. → Show an explicit loading notice and a retry action for failed initial loads. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

UI-05 — Late pagination responses could insert history from another chat; thread pagination could hide the main chat's earlier-message control. A l…: Late pagination responses could insert history from another chat; thread pagination could hide the main chat's earlier-message control. A late successful send could clear a newly selected conversation's draft. → Scope response updates to the conversation/thread generation, reset pagination when closing a thread, and preserve a draft edited while submission is pending. UI-06 — Header symbols and adjacent task actions were unclear or crowded.: Header symbols and adjacent task actions were unclear or crowded. → Use existing icon components for Memory & skills/Computer, truncate long titles, and wrap action rows with consistent gaps. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

C14 — Accumulated test groups and two UI bots cluttered actual usage: Issue/cause: Acceptance fixtures remained visible in the working roster. → Approach and outcome: Archive/remove 59 fixture groups while retaining saved records/outputs; delete the two fixture bots through lifecycle operations, preserving original bots/volumes and the already-created calendar effect. Add group removal with settled-work checks. [status: Owner-authorized cleanup verified]

The transcript does not establish a more specific selector-level root cause. → Approach and outcome: Correct response-action presentation; verify streaming, queued and failed states plus correct inspect/stop targets at five widths. [status: Responsive layout checks verified]

Separate noncollapsible roster sections consumed the available height. → Selected approach and fix: constrain/wrap content and restore responsive dialog sizing; collapsible roster sections with shared scrolling and retained controls. [status: Verified within stated scope, 2026-10-07. Category: UX/layout.]

decisions.decision: Ordinary messages are interpreted automatically; no message-intent dropdown, work selector or skill picker in the composer.
decisions.why: Owner rejected manual context selection as extra effort (T1-U54, C16).
decisions.tradeoffs: Misinterpretation is possible; corrections happen in natural chat.

decisions.decision: A shared application intake/controller interprets owner messages into validated operations and versioned work revisions before execution (Oct 13), replacing the first design where the responding model called hermbot_route_message.
decisions.why: Routing and execution were too coupled; changes, mixed messages and cross-bot owner updates needed handling above the harness (C28, TEMP-03/04).
decisions.alternatives: Model-side routing inside the executing bot; keyword classifier or separate classification model (rejected).
decisions.tradeoffs: Extra model call per message; finite evaluation coverage (24 cases).

decisions.decision: Work items are separate from executions; discussion/status/thanks create no work; revisions attach to the same item with separate execution trees and permissions.
decisions.why: Every message had become a sidebar work item (C15).

decisions.decision: Owner changes are durable revision commands delivered to active/waiting work; superseded requirements stop counting and affected undispatched drafts are retired.
decisions.why: A Redirect stayed pending while the manager waited (TEMP-04); obsolete requirement kept work at 2 of 4 (TEMP-07).

decisions.decision: Failed interpretation preserves the message and offers Retry interpretation; ambiguity asks in chat.
decisions.why: Never lose owner input.

decisions.decision: Automatic intake applies only to /api/v1/messages with intent auto; legacy intents and /api/v1/tasks keep compatibility.
decisions.why: Client compatibility and historical work not replayed.

pitfalls.text: C15 — Every ordinary user message became a work item: Issue/cause: Ordinary messages used the task endpoint and the sidebar listed root executions, conflating discussion, status, changes and assignments. → Approach and outcome: Separate work items from executions, automatically route ordinary messages and associate updates with existing work; retain visible failures without manufacturing assignments. [status: Implemented and historically verified; later interpretation defects remain]

C16 — Manual context-selection dropdown increased user effort: Issue/cause: The first interaction design exposed context/message classification choices to the user. → Approach and outcome: Remove the message-intent dropdown, work selector and inline classification controls; infer intent/context automatically and clarify only actual ambiguity. [status: Removed and verified]

C27 — Project chat temp2 exposed broader revision, coordination and result-quality problems: Issue/cause: Original T1-U102 reviewed 20 messages, 17 tasks and tool records; T1-U104 revisited the design causes. The individual findings are recovered in TEMP-01–TEMP-11 below, including a mistyped connection ID, rejected owner corrections, a pending Redirect, the 24-turn cap, DOCX delivery gaps and obsolete requirements. → Approach and outcome: Move owner intent application and versioned requirements into the application; maintain pending owner directions, current authorization, shared result bindings and execution reconciliation across bots. [status: General application change implemented; current gaps remain]

TEMP-03 — “Create a google doc ... do it” and “@scout follow that” attempted owner updates through Scout; ownership/grant checks rejected them, and t…: “Create a google doc ... do it” and “@scout follow that” attempted owner updates through Scout; ownership/grant checks rejected them, and they became discussion-only. → Cross-bot owner updates implemented and verified. Controller native proof verifies owner revision through another teammate without transferring management credentials. Later intake failures remain distinct and open. [status: Cross-bot owner updates implemented and verified.]

TEMP-04 — Redirect stayed pending while the manager waited on an upload whose prerequisite had been cancelled. Storing the correction did not wake/re…: Redirect stayed pending while the manager waited on an upload whose prerequisite had been cancelled. Storing the correction did not wake/reconcile waiting work. → Durable revision commands and dependency recovery implemented. Controller review includes settlement-race correction and waiting-manager checks. Historical cancelled operations remain preserved. [status: Durable revision commands and dependency recovery implemented.]

TEMP-11 — Application appended “this answer does not approve any external change”; Sage then attributed that policy statement to the owner, who had r…: Application appended “this answer does not approve any external change”; Sage then attributed that policy statement to the owner, who had requested Google Docs and Slack. → Provenance wording corrected. Answer continuation separates application policy from the actual authenticated answer; M14/M27 show remaining contextual-provenance gaps. Exact task authorization is recorded separately from commentary. [status: Provenance wording corrected.]

C27A — Implementation language made a systemic change sound like a one-task patch: Issue/cause: The phrase “first implementation slice” focused on DOCX-to-Google-Doc replacement. The owner correctly challenged the framing (T1-U107/U108/U109). → Approach and outcome: Rephrase architecture, implementation steps and regression scenarios distinctly. Build shared work revisions, recovery, authorization and artifact interfaces; retain the particular document change as one test case. [status: Communication corrected; systemic scope retained.]

C28 — Automatic interpretation did not robustly represent discussion, updates and new actions: Issue/cause: Routing and execution were too closely coupled; changes, mixed messages and independent objectives needed explicit handling above the harness. → Approach and outcome: Interpret owner messages into validated operations and current work revisions, allow scoped earlier-context lookup, preserve original provenance and apply changes transactionally. [status: Application intake/controller implemented and evaluated; M01/M10–M17/M24–M27 remain open]

pitfalls.text: C10 — Slack local OAuth and search-token setup were confusing: Issue/cause: Slack OAuth could not use the configured local HTTP callback; search required a separate user token rather than only the displayed bot token. → Approach and outcome: Private bot/user token fields, explicit local-HTTP guidance and HTTPS OAuth support when configured. [status: Resolved after owner action; error handling improved]

C12 — New GitHub account had no repository; selected repo later rejected issue access: Issue/cause: Initially there were no repositories. After repository creation, issue access required corrected token scope and reconnect. Empty issue/PR lists were legitimate data. → Approach and outcome: Owner created a test repository and updated access; preserve the failed run and use an explicit fresh read acceptance after reconnect. A successful read or draft is not proof that a private write completed. → Approach and outcome: Verify exact reads and frozen reviewed writes separately. pitfalls.text: C41 — Chat routine draft used a display name as a bot ID: Observed trigger: A real owner message asked Scout to prepare an inactive weekday routine. The interpreter returned a valid routine proposal with `bot_id=scout`, while Scout's database ID is `researcher`. The draft insert hit a foreign key, exhausted three intake attempts, and left the original message queued with a generic failure. No routine or future work was created by those failed attempts. → Fix: work_intake.py now lists eligible ID/name pairs, requires the model to use the ID, and resolves an unambiguous participant display name at application time. routines.py validates draft bot membership before writing. This leaves unknown or ambiguous names rejected as a routine-specific validation error. [status: Verified within the local routine scope. An active routine pointed at an archived conversation could resume silently if that conversation was restored before the next due time. A recurring connector effect's saved action was compared with its expected result, but its de… → Fix: routines.py cancels unstarted work in the same transaction as a revision edit/pause/archive, pauses routines when a destination becomes unavailable, and accepts a schedule alone for preview. product.py pauses active routines at the owner archive action, requiring explicit resume after restoration. routine_models.py requires the saved action and destination to match the expected external result. Routines.tsx sen… [status: Verified within the local routine scope. These were pre-release code review findings, not observed external provider failures.]

C44 — Result editing repeated a plain-HTTP browser API mistake: Root cause: The new editor copied `crypto.randomUUID()` from the time editor instead of reusing the existing HTTP-compatible `requestKey()` helper. The API can be absent on a nonsecure HTTP origin, making Add expected result fail. This is the same browser-context assumption recorded historically in C04, in another caller. → Fix: Use the shared helper based on cryptographically generated bytes in both forms. Keep identifiers in the existing UUID format. [status: Corrected in both the event-trigger and existing time-routine editors.]

Daily limits used receipt/creation time rather than actual admission time. Pending capacity was checked before coalescing reuse and combined occurrences lacked a member bound. Admission repeatedly selected the oldest blocked triggers, risking starvation, and acquired a convers… → Approach/fix: Keep immutable raw-body hashes for HTTP and stable logical-identity hashes for polling; count `admitted_at`; reuse eligible occurrences before capacity checks and cap them at 100 members; rotate blocked admission times; take destination locks without waiting; explicitly normalize tombstones and compare signature bytes; use authoritative work/execution identities in history; derive disconnected status f… [status: Corrected and covered by targeted regressions in the Phase 5.2 build.]

The Changes API subsequently returned versions 6 and 7 under the unchanged name; two unwanted event reports ran before the owner's real rename. The owner's rename itself produced one correct report. The acceptance verifier initially could have counted a creation echo as positive input; it now requires the explicit external-change m… → Fix: Persist a fingerprint of the observed name, MIME type, modification time, parent IDs and trash/removal state. Skip version-only changes with the same prior fingerprint. Request those fields directly in new Drive create/upload receipts and correlate equal receipt state despite a different server version. The fresh test proved conversion changes modification time too, so state comparison alone did not close the i… [status: Fixed and deployed locally. All five provider checks, including the separately approved Google Doc and its read-only creation verification, pass. The original failures remain recorded.]

C49 — A full daily allowance deferred self-event reconciliation: Observed: The fresh Doc's initially unmatched creation event remained pending behind the three-run daily allowance even after a definitive own-write proof was available. No duplicate provider effect occurred, but normal admission could not classify the event as ignored that day. → Fix: Validate the event/source and check own-write correlation before applying the daily admission cap. Keep the cap before any real task creation. Backlog, authority and expiry protections remain intact. [status: Fixed and verified locally during the final Drive acceptance.]

decisions.decision: Any ordinary bot becomes a manager only via an owner-issued scoped grant (targets, operations, budget, duration); task-bound by default, standing grants for ongoing.
decisions.why: Owner asked for orchestration plus lifecycle (P-U8) and chose 'Tasks and lifecycle'.
decisions.alternatives: Task orchestration only; full approved administration incl. delete/tool/connection changes.
decisions.tradeoffs: Lifecycle proposals require exact owner review.

decisions.decision: Managers cannot self-escalate, approve on the owner's behalf, read private histories/memory/credentials, gain connector access, or delete bots; stopping a runtime needs separate authority.
decisions.why: Least privilege.

decisions.decision: Lifecycle proposals show exact config/prior state/resources/affected work; edits create fresh approvals; approved ops go through a durable supervisor outbox; manager resumes after provisioning; retries reuse original identity.
decisions.why: Stale proposals and duplicate provisioning risk.

decisions.decision: Recurring/event management binds an optional {grant_id, targets, operations} object; server freezes scope at admission; each use intersects with the current grant; no automatic alternate grant.
decisions.why: A schedule must not mint authority (IAM PassRole analogy); grants can expire/revoke between occurrences.
decisions.alternatives: Copy grant snapshot; auto-pick another valid grant.
decisions.tradeoffs: Expired authority pauses definitions until owner resumes.

decisions.decision: Recurring runs may only delegate/inspect/steer/cancel/reassign; lifecycle operations stay manual.
decisions.why: Avoid automated lifecycle changes.

decisions.decision: Automated work keeps a static indexed management_work_item_id; authority/budget/locks/overlap/stop use it.
decisions.why: Cosmetic reassociation could detach scope (C51).

decisions.decision: One aggregate active-time budget per occurrence shared by manager, contributors, peer replies and retries; only owner Continue adds budget.
decisions.why: Children shouldn't each assume the whole allowance.

decisions.decision: Separate controls: pause future starts vs stop current run vs both; revocation stops all live work using the grant.
decisions.why: Temporal: schedule pause ≠ workflow stop.
decisions.tradeoffs: Revoking a shared grant affects other routines.

pitfalls.text: P2-09 — Approved creation retry incorrectly spent or checked a second creation budget; a settled manager could reuse old authority.: Approved creation retry incorrectly spent or checked a second creation budget; a settled manager could reuse old authority. → Recheck live authority without consuming another creation, reject settled manager operations and stale/source-busy retries. [status: Historically corrected within source review scope]

C50 — Task inspection code broke the workspace state endpoint: Observed: The first 5.3 live acceptance attempt received HTTP 500 from `/api/v1/state` before creating fixture work. → Approach/fix: Keep enrichment in task inspection and test authenticated workspace state plus the narrowed task scope together. The first failed attempt created no test work; later native demonstrations ran through the corrected endpoint. [status: Fixed; API regression and deployed state/browser checks pass.]

C51 — Display reassociation could detach automated work from its occurrence: Observed/design defect: Tracing owner message correction showed that mutable work/intent fields could be cleared while the admitted execution continued. A lookup using only those fields would lose recurring scope and shared budget/stop coverage. → Approach/fix: Add the indexed static `management_work_item_id` for admitted automated work, freezing scope on the occurrence's work record. Use it for authority, budget, locking, overlap and owned stop. Preserve normal cosmetic correction behavior. Do not infer authority from thread proximity or attach unrelated owner discussion to an occurrence. [status: Fixed and verified with reclassification, accounting, continuation, overlap and cancellation regressions.]

C52 — Selected cancellation authority implicitly depended on inspection: Observed/design defect: A valid selected operation subset could pass configuration validation and then fail because cancel/steer/reassign reused an inspection helper. → Approach/fix: Pass the actual requested operation through the shared owned-descendant check. Keep inspect as the default for true inspection and retain separate manager/grant validation at mutation callers. [status: Fixed and verified; delegate+cancel permits its owned cancellation boundary and rejects ordinary inspection.]

C53 — Native completion prose could misstate recurring success: Observed/design defect: A manager could end a native turn without accepted required results while the execution itself recorded completion. Original-root-only failure counting also missed later successful repair of the same occurrence. → Approach/fix: Reject final acceptance while required or optional automated work is unsettled. If a manager ends without accepted required results, record explicit failure and stop remaining owned execution. Count definite failures from current settled occurrence work/results. Advance incremental windows only from verified compatible success, including equivalent grant renewal, and after attempts/effects settle. [status: Fixed with missing-result/failure regressions, final acceptance guards and verified native contribution receipts.]

C54 — Managed reply admission could invert revocation's lock order: Observed/design defect: The newly authority-bound peer path could validate/hold a grant before acquiring its work lock, while revocation acquired work before updating the grant. Those two orders can wait on each other. → Approach/fix: Claim canonical work/root nonblockingly before validating authority in peer admission. Align dispatch/revoke canonical work identity and skip a busy occurrence for a later pass. Replies inherit scope/run/thread/budget; revocation cancels owned pending execution and messages without fabricating effect receipts. [status: Fixed; concurrent revoke/claim and locked-occurrence peer-admission regressions pass.]

pitfalls.text: C55 — Push timeout extension changed the existing connector deadline: Observed/design defect: Adding a push-specific timeout captured the module timeout constant in a default argument; changing the runtime test deadline no longer interrupted the response. → Approach/fix: Resolve the optional timeout at call time, retain existing raw-response callers and add explicit push response metadata through the public library session hook. Preserve pinned public-address sockets, original TLS hostname, no redirects/proxies and bounded response reads. [status: Fixed; the original slow-drip transport regression and cumulative 638-test suite pass.]

C56 — Catch-up eligibility could use unrelated unread work: Observed/design defect: A summary whose own covered questions had resolved could still send because a different unread question existed elsewhere. → Approach/fix: Recheck actual covered item/version references and their freshness; overflow summaries alone represent general fresh backlog. Do not self-merge a summary into itself. [status: Fixed with current-member, empty-digest and read-before-send regressions.]

C57 — Quiet-period and overflow replacement could repeat or lose interruption: Observed/design defect: Repeated local hours could yield two quiet-end keys. Preference changes could suppress a pending summary after its individual records were marked covered; overflow-only backlog had no item row to recreate. → Approach/fix: Key quiet periods by explicit local period/policy/browser generation; retain fresh covered members and one overflow obligation across policy replacement. Reserve one of 1,000 pending positions for overflow and count actual dispatch attempts for the three-per-minute cap. Do not replay stale work or drop the in-app record. [status: Fixed; DST-fold, covered-member policy replacement, saturation, burst and overflow-only replacement regressions pass.]

C58 — Slow push could delay the attention projector: Observed/design defect: The first notification worker performed projection and outbound delivery sequentially, so a slow vendor could hold new inbox state behind HTTP. → Approach/fix: Independent projection and sending pumps run inside the same small control-network service, without model credentials or bot slots. [status: Fixed; a blocked-send regression verifies a real database question still projects concurrently.]

C59 — Retention could reverse the delivery lock order: Observed/design defect: Delivery completion acquired delivery before subscription/preferences, while initial reconciliation/retention held preferences/subscriptions before updating expired deliveries. An expiring in-flight record can complete that cycle. → Approach/fix: Commit maintenance families independently; derive server-key health from subscription state rather than updating preferences while holding a delivery lock. Use fenced short claims and send outside transactions. [status: Corrected by connected-path review; cumulative/concurrency checks pass. A production deadlock was not reproduced.]

C61 — A browser endpoint alone did not identify the registration generation: Observed/design defect: The same endpoint could be re-registered with new browser keys without changing its generation. An old completion could then affect a replacement registration. → Approach/fix: Fence by the endpoint, key material, configured origin/server key and registration generation. Retain safe replaced records, retire only the failing current generation and revoke the current browser explicitly on logout. Normal session expiry remains separate. [status: Fixed; encrypted registration/key rotation, stale lease, per-device error and current-browser logout regressions pass.]

Vendor acceptance alone does not establish browser receipt or an OS banner. → Investigation and cleanup: Temporary opaque-delivery receipts, browser checks and a local display test were deployed to distinguish delivery stages. After confirming the configuration fix, the owner requested their removal. Removed the diagnostic UI/state, automatic browser checks, receipt routes/schema/settings fields, extra push-payload field and diagnostic-specific tests. Retain ordinary push, preferences, regist… [status: Resolved by owner configuration, October 26, 2026. The owner enabled notifications for Chrome and confirmed that notifications now work. No application push-transport defect was established.]

pitfalls.text: C31 — Simple tools repeatedly took 120–240 seconds: Issue/cause: Exclusive Hermbot admission could hold a lock inside a later callback waiting for an earlier Hermes start-order entry that was itself waiting on that lock. → Approach and outcome: Shared per-callback admission plus exclusive takeover drain; preserve epoch, stop and exception semantics without changing Hermes. H01 — Tool admission/start-order circular wait: Cause: Hermbot held an exclusive per-bot lock around the Hermes callback. A later callback could hold it while waiting in Hermes's start-order gate for an earlier callback blocked on the same lock. The original takeover design assumed that exclusive foreground-tool admission was compatible with harness parallel execution. → Selected approach and fix: shared admission for each bot callback; takeover closes new admission and drains admitted callbacks exclusively before human input. Preserve viewer/epoch checks and release admission correctly on exceptions/process exit. Hermes source remains unchanged. [status: Verified within stated scope, 2026-10-13. Category: concurrency/integration. Impact: simple parallel tools waited approximately 120 seconds each.]

topology.text: Compose services: postgres, storage (MinIO), api, worker, event-worker, notification-worker, supervisor, runtime-image helper; dynamic hermbot-bot-* containers owned by supervisor; legacy fixed hermes-* services under 'legacy' profile.
Networks: control for DB/storage/workers; per-bot networks joined by api and worker; only 127.0.0.1:8780 published.
Three layers from the planning thread: UI, product backend, Hermes adapter + Hermes runtime; Hermes authoritative for execution.

control-vs-data-plane.text: Control plane: FastAPI + PostgreSQL own coordination, receipts, leases, controls, approvals, projections; supervisor owns container lifecycle. Data/execution plane: each Hermes runtime owns its agent loop and native session history.
Runtime integration only through authenticated Runs API, supported plugin hooks/middleware and Hermbot's private per-runtime adapter (desktop, knowledge, routine wake).

isolation.text: Per-bot network, identity token, native API credential and data/workspace/browser volumes; never mount the same Hermes DB in multiple runtimes.
Runtime hardening: read-only root FS, root-owned plugin mount, CapDrop ALL + no-new-privileges, non-root gateway; no Docker socket.
Boundary is a trusted single-owner tool-admission boundary, not OS sandboxing of arbitrary background processes.
Stronger VM-per-bot isolation researched and deferred until after Phases 1-8.

durability.text: PostgreSQL is queue/outbox/receipt store (no broker); artifacts immutable in MinIO with checksums; supervisor receipts fsynced on its own volume.
Never replay uncertain effects; reconcile with receipts/provider state; no universal exactly-once claims.
Event collector commits events and cursor per page together and acknowledges after commit; attention uses transactional dirty hints rather than a sequence watermark.

concurrency.text: One active/uncertain attempt per bot, three concurrent executions; waiting parents release slots.

Lock discipline recorded across reviews: NOWAIT shared bot lock for admission, workspace-before-source, root-before-grant, nonblocking destination share lock, work/root before grant, domain->attention->delivery, independent maintenance commits.
Tool admission: shared nonblocking per-callback admission with exclusive takeover drain.

workers.text: worker: durable dispatch, continuations, recovery, lifecycle outbox; event-worker: provider collection only; notification-worker: attention projection and Web Push with independent pumps.

recovery.text: Worker restart reconnects existing native run identities; only desired-running runtimes start; stop.py preserves volumes.
Phase 5 exit verified API/task/event/notification worker restarts preserved task, run, attempt and session IDs.
Unknown connector outcomes: Reconcile outcome or close as Outcome unknown; retry/reassign blocked.

security.text: Owner token login with opaque revocable cookies; secrets encrypted with CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY; API access logs disabled; validation errors omit inputs.
Outbound HTTP (link import, connectors, MCP, Web Push) pinned to validated public IPs, TLS to original hostname, no redirects/proxies, absolute deadlines.
Open: ordinary-chat secrets propagate to task/attempt records (M28).

observability.text: Activity distinguishes observed tool activity, last progress and runtime contact; contact alone isn't progress; optional execution assessments.
Issue register is manual; no automatic runtime failure capture; intake failure details discarded (M25); Phase 7.2 correlated logs pending.

scaling-spof.text: Single machine, single owner; computer and Docker must stay awake; no remote wake; single PostgreSQL/MinIO.
Release validation target: ten registered bots and three active tasks; one desktop per bot not all concurrent.
